object_description: long building with an open two-storey base and three teaching floors
design_condition: The building runs along the main street, is set back to widen the sidewalk and passage, places sports halls at its ends, and forms a large, publicly usable courtyard connected to an upper terrace.

positive.statement: The simple building figure respects the surrounding existing buildings to a high degree.

position.rationale: Simple elongated mass is clearly corroborated across the rectangular top and elevations.

positive.statement: The arrangement creates the greatest possible open space between the neighboring buildings and the new building.

position.rationale: Setback-related open space is anchored along the building’s long lateral edge.

positive.statement: The passage, courtyard and sports-hall arrangement produces a strong openness toward the urban space.

position.rationale: Central opening-like top pattern and end masses support a constrained courtyard and passage anchor.

positive.statement: The courtyard is well integrated into the neighborhood and supports dual use by the school and public.

position.rationale: Central void/open zone is visible between the elongated building’s longitudinal masses.

positive.statement: The clear building structure and construction with supports and panels create a high level of flexibility.

position.rationale: Regular vertical and horizontal structural rhythm is visible throughout the facade elevations.

positive.statement: The suspended platform creates spatial richness and sequences that merge without corridors.

position.rationale: Elevations clearly show upper massing suspended above the open lower base.

positive.statement: The large terrace connects to the courtyard and adds an unusual spatial opportunity.

position.rationale: Upper open platform is approximated beside the central courtyard-facing portion.

positive.statement: The covered access areas and courtyard-side lounge are attractive and work well in school operations.

position.target: covered access areas and courtyard-side lounge
position.rationale: Ground-level edge adjacent to the central opening provides a plausible covered-access anchor.

positive.statement: The teaching floors are well lit, clear and furnished with well-proportioned classrooms.

position.rationale: Repeated upper-level bands are clearly visible, though individual classrooms are not isolated.

positive.statement: The special classrooms are prominently arranged and positively enliven the street space.

position.rationale: Street-facing outer edge is constrained from the stated placement, without identifiable classroom markers.

positive.statement: The spatial program is implemented efficiently.

position.rationale: Overall modular building organization is visible, while program efficiency itself is non-geometric.

positive.statement: Daylight use is good and the ventilation principle is conceptually sensible.

position.rationale: Upper envelope and open courtyard provide approximate anchors for daylight and ventilation strategies.

positive.statement: The separated usage units enable a solid structural fire-protection concept.

position.rationale: Modular upper massing suggests separated units, but fire compartments are not directly visible.

positive.statement: The diverse entrances and exits support an open and communicative institution.

position.rationale: Ground-level perimeter near the passage provides a plausible entrance anchor.

negative.statement: The scarce core areas inadequately meet the requirements for sanitary and service spaces.

position.rationale: Interior service spaces are not visible; a constrained anchor is placed within the lower building zone.

negative.statement: The structural concept has weaknesses because some facade supports are not directly supported by the framework.

position.rationale: External supports are visibly repeated along the facade, though load-path defects are not geometrically testable.

negative.statement: The rigid ceiling-to-facade connections are not convincing because of temperature deformation and thermal requirements.

position.rationale: Upper facade junction provides a constrained anchor for the stated connection concern.

negative.statement: The earthquake bracing still needs to be checked in the longitudinal direction.

position.rationale: Longitudinal structural system follows the elongated building, but bracing is not individually visible.

negative.statement: The high gray energy per square meter results from the lack of compactness and complex supporting concept.

position.target: high gray energy per square meter
position.rationale: Embodied-energy performance is a whole-building judgment without a useful single spatial marker.

negative.statement: The external supporting facade is cost-intensive and challenging in terms of building physics.

position.rationale: External supporting facade is visible as the repeated perimeter structure along the elevations.

negative.statement: The facade has not yet been mastered structurally and physically.

position.rationale: Long facade surfaces are directly visible, while structural and physical mastery is evaluative.

negative.statement: The above-average envelope and window proportions increase the technical and economic demands.

position.rationale: Facade proportions are visible across the long elevations, including repeated window and support rhythms.
